key_cases.case_name: Burney v. Kansas Department of Social & Rehabilitation Services
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a negligence verdict for a substitute teacher who had been investigated for child abuse, holding that SRS owes no duty to an alleged abuser, that there is no special relationship between the agency and a suspect, and that both the decision whether to open a file and the manner of conducting a child abuse investigation are discretionary functions immune under the Kansas Tort Claims Act.
key_cases.relevance: Someone wrongly named in a substantiated finding cannot sue the agency in negligence for the investigation that produced it.
key_cases.quote: we hold that in investigating child abuse cases, SRS owes no duty to the alleged abuser

key_cases.case_name: T.H. v. University of Kansas Hospital Authority
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of a malpractice suit against a physician who reported suspected sexual abuse, holding that K.S.A. 38-2223(f) immunizes reporters who negligently misdiagnose abuse and that the immunity is lost only if the plaintiff pleads facts supporting actual malice, meaning a specific intent to injure.
key_cases.relevance: A family harmed by an erroneous abuse determination generally has no civil remedy against the reporting professional absent pleaded malice.
key_cases.quote: In sum, we find that K.S.A. 2015 Supp. 38-2223(f) provides immunity to doctors who negligently misdiagnose child abuse

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the CINC adjudication, holding that the Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause does not apply in CINC proceedings, that a child's hearsay statements were admissible under K.S.A. 60-460(a) even though the State did not call her in its case in chief, and that the district judge's standing offer to summon the child for cross-examination satisfied whatever confrontation right due process supplied.
key_cases.relevance: A finding that a child is in need of care may rest on the child's out-of-court statements relayed by a counselor, investigator and detective, so long as the declarant is made available for cross-examination.
key_cases.quote: Any right that a civil litigant can claim to confrontation and cross-examination is grounded in the Due Process Clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the CINC adjudication, holding that clear and convincing evidence in Kansas means evidence sufficient to establish that the truth of the facts asserted is highly probable, disapproving all contrary holdings, and that an appellate court reviewing such a determination asks only whether a rational factfinder could have found it highly probable on the evidence viewed most favorably to the State.
key_cases.relevance: This is the load-bearing Kansas definition of the burden the State must carry to obtain a finding that a child is in need of care.
key_cases.quote: We agree with those courts that have essentially defined clear and convincing evidence as that which is sufficient to establish that the truth of the facts asserted is "highly probable."

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: A later finding is allowed only if a delay is requested by law enforcement, a county or district attorney, the court, or health or mental health professionals, or exceptional circumstances are documented in the case file (DCF PPM 2511 C.). An allowable late finding requires the Child Protection Specialist to enter "Allowable Delay" on the PPS 2011 Case Findings Section IV on or before the case finding due date; if the finding is late for a reason not allowable under PPM 2511 C., the specialist shall document with the finding: "The case finding is delayed due to a non-allowable reason per policy." (DCF PPM 2531 E.)
